title: Mṛtyave svāhā: two oblations to Death
theme: Two oblations of ghee are offered to Death, each with the words ‘to Death, svāhā’.

words.context: The anonymous commentator: «येन म्रियन्ते प्राणिनः स मृत्युस्तस्मै» — Death is that by which living beings die

words.meaning: svāhā (the call with which an oblation is given)
words.context: The anonymous commentator: «स्वाहा सकृत्गृहीतमिदमाज्यं सुहुतमस्तु» — may this ghee, taken once, be well offered

morphology.note: Dative singular of mṛtyu, the case of the deity to whom an oblation is given.

translation.literal: To Death, svāhā! To Death, svāhā!
translation.readable: To Death — svāhā. To Death — svāhā.

syntax: Two identical formulas, each a dative of the deity and the call svāhā, with no verb.

metre.name: prose
metre.note: A yajus formula, not verse: 8 syllables as printed (mṛtyave svāhā twice).

beginner: This is the shortest anuvāka in this part of the Upaniṣad: two offerings, each made with the words "to Death, svāhā". "Svāhā" is the call with which an offering is poured into the sacred fire. The old commentator explains that the formula is said twice because two offerings are made, and that both are offered to Death, that by which living beings die. He also explains where these formulas belong: from here on come offering formulas for removing wrongdoing, and the person who wishes to be rid of wrongdoing performs the offering according to the rules of his own household manual and offers the main oblations with these words. The edition reports this as the commentator’s account of the rite; it makes no claim about what the offering achieves.
analogy: Like two stones laid on a cairn by a traveller: the same gesture twice, each one counted.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: Two oblations, each with the words ‘to Death, svāhā’.

commentary.q: What is the rite, according to the commentator?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator says that from here offering formulas for removing every sin are taught: «अथेदानीं पापमात्रनिवर्हणार्था होममन्त्रा उच्यन्ते». One who wishes to be rid of sin performs the preliminary rites according to his own domestic manual, «तेन स्वगृह्योक्तविधिना», and offers the main oblations with these formulas. The formula is repeated to mark two oblations, «आहुतिद्वयद्योतनार्था मन्त्रावृत्तिः», and both go to Death: «इदमाहुतिद्वयं मृत्युदेवत्यम्».

schools.disagreement: No Vedānta-school commentary on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s commentary on the Mahānārāyaṇa is not among them). The anonymous bhāṣya explains the words and the rite; it does not argue an Advaita, Viśiṣṭādvaita or Dvaita position here, so the edition gives none.

contemporary.text: An offering made to Death itself, plainly and twice, treats death neither as an enemy to be fought nor as something unmentionable, but as a power to be acknowledged by name. This is a modern reflection on the passage, not part of its traditional meaning.

reflect.beginner: Why might a rite name Death directly instead of avoiding the word?
reflect.deeper: The commentator places these formulas at the start of a series for removing wrongdoing. Why would an offering to Death come first?
reflect.practice: Once today, speak plainly about something you usually avoid naming.

references.text: No comment of Sāyaṇa’s or Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara’s on this anuvāka is in the edition’s sources: Sāyaṇa’s anuvākas 52–57 are missing from the digital text used here, and neither commentary file glosses these words; the edition’s concordance maps give no anuvāka of theirs for it. The anonymous bhāṣya is the only commentary quoted.
